As I see it, there is no way that we can know that the situation you
describe will not become a major problem, especially as the distinction
between "human" and "machine" blurs. What if you could take a pill that
would grow a biochip memory module in your brain so that you would never
need to forget anything? Or a similar calculation module so that you would
instantly know the answer to any math problem? Or for that matter to any
ethical problem (subject to preprogrammed ethical schemes in the chip)? And
this is just scratching the surface....

As far as machine-made decisions yielding better results, try to land a
space shuttle without a computer. This is a case of do or die, not just
"better". Similar examples abound.

John
